title: Shared Shell State Across Windows
body: What every OpenKaava window has to agree on. The shell runs in more than one window: the main one, plus a real OS window for anything dragged out of it. The layout cannot be window-local because two windows disagreeing would be a visible bug. So the layout lives in the backend and each window is a projection of it subscribing to shell:state. Nothing is copied between windows, which means nothing can drift out of sync.
